scope_note: Funding research for Bancroft Boxing & Grappling (BBG, for-profit gym), Cottage Country Combat League (CCCL, for-profit amateur MMA promoter), Second Chance (planned nonprofit, not yet incorporated) and families of BBG kids. Facts below were checked on the cited source pages between Oct 17 and Oct 18, 2026. 'eligible_now' means: yes = BBG/CCCL/families/a grassroots group can apply today if the stated conditions are met; after nonprofit = Second Chance must first be an incorporated not-for-profit (non-share-capital corporation); after charity = Second Chance must be a CRA registered charity or other qualified donee (or apply through a qualified-donee trustee where the funder allows it).

programs.name: Canada Summer Jobs 2027 (private-sector employer rate)
programs.who_can_apply: Not-for-profits, public-sector employers, and private-sector (for-profit) employers with 50 or fewer full-time employees
programs.what_it_funds: Wage subsidy for summer jobs for youth aged 15 to 30 (e.g., youth program assistant coaches, camp staff, event and marketing assistants)
programs.amount: Private sector: up to 50% of the provincial adult minimum hourly wage; mandatory employment-related costs (MERCs) are not reimbursed. Ontario's adult minimum wage is $17.95/hour from Oct 1, 2026, so roughly $8.98/hour per youth (estimate; the rate CSJ applies may differ)
programs.intake: CSJ 2027 call opens October 27, 2026 at 9:00 am ET (canada.ca, modified Sept 29, 2026). Closing date not yet posted (the 2026 call ran Nov 4 to Dec 11, 2025).
programs.status: open since Oct 27, 2026 (close date not posted yet)
programs.matching: Employer pays the remaining ~50% of wages plus all MERCs
programs.how_to_apply: Apply online through the CSJ applicant guide's 'Apply now' section once the call opens Oct 27, 2026
programs.notes: Cody wants a funded summer student (Cody, Oct 20, 2026). The form's first question asks for the payroll (RP) number, and BBG only has a business number: open the CRA payroll account now (CSJ opened Oct 27). The student can't replace volunteers and BBG must manage the job itself, so the draft is a gym-only job. Draft: 'CSJ 2027 Application Draft' (Command Centre). 2026 job rules (2027 rules likely similar): 30 to 40 hours/week, 6 to 16 consecutive weeks, start no earlier than Apr 20 and end by Aug 29. CFIB notes a CRA payroll deductions account is needed before hiring. Riding local priorities for Hastings-Lennox and Addington-Tyendinaga in 2026 included community events and local/regional tourism development (good fit for CCCL); confirm Bancroft's riding. If BBG and CCCL are the same legal entity they count as one employer.

programs.name: Canada Summer Jobs 2027 (not-for-profit employer rate)
programs.who_can_apply: Not-for-profit organizations (also public and small private employers at the lower rate)
programs.what_it_funds: Summer jobs for youth aged 15 to 30, e.g., youth employment outreach or program assistant roles
programs.amount: Up to 100% of the provincial adult minimum hourly wage plus eligible MERCs
programs.intake: 2027 call opens October 27, 2026 at 9:00 am ET; close date not yet posted
programs.status: open since Oct 27, 2026 (close date not posted yet)
programs.matching: None required at the not-for-profit rate (up to 100%)
programs.how_to_apply: Apply online via the CSJ applicant guide once the call opens
programs.notes: Second Chance would need to be an established not-for-profit employer at application time; the 2027 call likely closes in early-to-mid December 2026, which is probably too soon unless incorporation is done within weeks. Plan for CSJ 2028 otherwise.

programs.name: Canada Small Business Financing Program (CSBFP)
programs.funder: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (delivered by banks and credit unions)
programs.who_can_apply: Small businesses or start-ups operating in Canada with gross annual revenues of $10 million or less (farming excluded)
programs.what_it_funds: Government-backed loans for equipment, leasehold improvements, real property, intangible assets and working capital; lines of credit
programs.amount: Up to $1.15M per borrower: term loans up to $1M (max $500K for leasehold improvements and equipment, of which up to $150K for intangibles and working capital); lines of credit up to $150K
programs.intake: Continuous
programs.matching: Loan, not a grant. 2% registration fee; interest capped (floating term loans at lender prime + 3%; lines of credit prime + 5%)
programs.how_to_apply: Ask a financial officer at your bank or credit union for a CSBFP loan; the lender approves and registers it
programs.notes: Cody is thinking about a new or bigger space (Cody, Oct 20, 2026): CSBFP loans can cover leasehold improvements and equipment as well as gear. Good route for gym equipment (mats, ring, bags) or a cage/ring and production gear for CCCL shows.

programs.name: Futurpreneur Core Startup Program (with BDC)
programs.funder: Futurpreneur Canada (national non-profit) with Business Development Bank of Canada
programs.who_can_apply: Entrepreneurs aged 18 to 39 (Canadian citizen or PR) whose business is pre-startup or has less than a year of significant sales
programs.what_it_funds: Start-up loans plus up to two years of 1:1 mentorship
programs.amount: Up to $75,000 total: up to $25,000 from Futurpreneur (RBC prime + 3%, capped at 9%) and up to $50,000 from BDC (BDC floating base rate + 1.65%); interest-only first year
programs.intake: Continuous
programs.matching: Loan, not a grant; 1% loan management fee on the Futurpreneur portion
programs.how_to_apply: Sign up on futurpreneur.ca to be contacted, or submit a business plan and 24-month cash flow through the MyFP portal
programs.notes: Cody is 18-39 and runs BBG and CCCL as two businesses (Cody, Oct 20, 2026). CCCL's first show was May 2, 2026, so CCCL has under a year of sales and may qualify; BBG opened in 2025, so it probably doesn't. Only fits if the owner is 39 or younger and the business is new (CCCL ran its first show recently and may qualify; BBG only if it has had less than a year of significant sales).

programs.name: Ontario Job Grant (formerly Canada-Ontario Job Grant)
programs.funder: Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development (Employment Ontario)
programs.who_can_apply: Private-sector (for-profit) and non-profit employers with a physical Ontario location that have operated in Ontario for at least one year
programs.what_it_funds: Third-party training for existing staff or new hires (e.g., coaching, first aid, safe sport, business or marketing courses delivered by an eligible training provider)
programs.amount: Up to $10,000 per trainee; up to $15,000 per previously unemployed new hire with no minimum employer contribution
programs.intake: Year-round; ministry currently accepting applications involving 25 or fewer participants
programs.matching: Employers with under 100 employees pay at least one-sixth of training costs (no contribution for unemployed new hires)
programs.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Employment Ontario Ontario Job Grant portal (one application at a time)
programs.notes: Not now: BBG has no payroll employees and its coaches are volunteers (Cody, Oct 20, 2026), so there's no one for the grant to train. Look again once BBG has staff on payroll. Training must come from an approved third-party provider with an Ontario presence and 2+ years delivering that training (colleges, universities, registered career colleges, union training centres, sector councils, industry associations). Legally required training is excluded. Second Chance qualifies as an employer only after it exists for a year and has staff.

programs.name: Rural Ontario Development (ROD) Program: Business Development stream
programs.who_can_apply: Small brick-and-mortar businesses in rural Ontario with 1 to 20 employees on payroll (excluding owners); incorporated, partnership, sole proprietorship or co-op; must pay commercial/industrial/agricultural property tax directly or through rent
programs.what_it_funds: Project types: market development, cyber security, succession planning, accessibility improvements. Eligible costs: professional fees, technology, marketing and promotion, minor capital for accessibility, training
programs.amount: 35% of project costs, up to $10,000 (minimum request $1,000)
programs.intake: Third period closed Oct 1, 2026. Fourth period: Jan 18 to Feb 25, 2027, 5 pm ET (subject to change)
programs.how_to_apply: Complete the PDF application in Adobe Acrobat and email it to RODProgram@ontario.ca; be registered on Transfer Payment Ontario
programs.notes: Not now: BBG has no payroll employees (Cody, Oct 20, 2026), and ROD needs 1 to 20 (owners don't count). If BBG puts someone on payroll before the Jan 18 to Feb 25, 2027 window, check again; it would also need to be registered on Transfer Payment Ontario (Cody isn't sure it is). First-come, first-served; only one successful ROD application per business ever. The latest application form lists market development, cyber, succession and accessibility projects, not general equipment. Owners do not count toward the 1-20 employee test, so BBG needs at least one payroll employee. CCCL likely fails the brick-and-mortar test unless it has its own commercial premises. Business-stream guidelines: https://www.ontario.ca/document/rural-ontario-development-program-rod-guidelines-business-development

programs.name: Rural Ontario Development (ROD) Program: community streams (workforce development, attraction and retention; economic diversification)
programs.who_can_apply: Municipalities, Indigenous communities and organizations, local services boards and not-for-profit organizations in rural Ontario
programs.what_it_funds: Workforce development, attraction and retention projects (fits employer partnerships and job-readiness work); also strategies and plans, economic diversification, and capacity-building events
programs.amount: Workforce stream: up to 50% cost share, up to $150,000. Strategies/plans: 50% up to $50,000. Capacity-building events: 35% up to $10,000
programs.intake: Fourth period Jan 18 to Feb 25, 2027, 5 pm ET (subject to change)
programs.matching: Applicant covers 50% (65% for events and infrastructure streams)
programs.how_to_apply: Email application to RODprogram@ontario.ca during an intake period
programs.notes: Second Chance's workforce work (job skills for people leaving the justice system) fits this stream once it's incorporated. Second Chance must be an incorporated not-for-profit before the February 2027 deadline to use this window; otherwise a partner municipality or nonprofit could lead.

programs.name: Skills Development Fund (SDF) Training Stream
programs.funder: Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development
programs.who_can_apply: Ontario employers (including for-profit), non-profit organizations, employer/industry associations, unions, municipalities and others; must be a legal entity operating in Ontario
programs.what_it_funds: Workforce projects: training, tools and wraparound supports, including for groups facing barriers such as youth 15-29 and justice-involved individuals; wage subsidies and training stipends
programs.amount: No set minimum or maximum; ministry first considers projects with budgets over $150,000. Wage subsidies and stipends capped at $5,000 per participant
programs.intake: Round 6 ran Jul 29 to Oct 1, 2025; the ontario.ca page says the application period has closed. Next round not announced
programs.matching: Cost-sharing or in-kind contributions are scored (5%) but not required; admin costs capped at 15%
programs.how_to_apply: Apply through Transfer Payment Ontario when a new round opens
programs.notes: Second Chance's focus (job skills and work experience for people leaving the justice system) is the kind of project SDF funds; partner with an established employment agency for the first round. Round 6 guide: https://forms.mgcs.gov.on.ca/dataset/5f0dd16c-f826-4cc4-822e-42e82c78b991/resource/5bdff2a4-18a5-4f7d-bb59-6e0ff7a030fd/download/sdf-ts-r6-application-guide-final-english.pdf. Big, competitive projects; a new Second Chance would do better as a partner to an established employment agency.

programs.name: Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund: Stream 2 (New Builds / Signature New Builds)
programs.who_can_apply: Municipalities, Indigenous communities, local services boards, not-for-profits, and for-profit organizations that operate or manage a space offering sport or recreation programming (new builds only)
programs.what_it_funds: New sport and recreation infrastructure, including repurposing or expanding existing structures to create net-new facilities
programs.amount: Up to $10 million (more for Signature New Builds); no minimum stated
programs.intake: Applications due Tuesday, December 22, 2026, 4 pm ET
programs.matching: For-profit provincial share capped at 25%; applicant covers the rest. Cannot stack with other Ontario funding for the same project
programs.how_to_apply: Apply per the CSRIF guidelines on ontario.ca (contact csrif@ontario.ca)
programs.notes: Cody is thinking about a new or bigger gym space (Cody, Oct 20, 2026). Stream 2 only funds new builds and asks for audited financial statements, which is a big cost for a small sole proprietorship (BBG's sales are under $50k a year). Long shot; Dec 22, 2026 deadline. Only worth it if BBG plans a new or expanded facility. Requires audited financial statements and a corporate structure document for for-profits. Projects must finish within 36 months and by Mar 31, 2030. Stream 1 (repairs) excludes for-profits. Program page: https://ontario.ca/communitysportfund

programs.name: Starter Company Plus (Hastings County delivery)
programs.funder: Government of Ontario, delivered by the Small Business Centre at the Quinte Business Development Centre (Belleville)
programs.who_can_apply: Ontario residents 18+, not in school full-time, starting, expanding or buying a business; the Belleville centre serves businesses registered in Hastings County, Prince Edward County, Lennox and Addington, Quinte West and Belleville
programs.what_it_funds: Business training, mentoring and a start-up/expansion grant
programs.amount: Grant up to $5,000
programs.intake: 2026 local intake ran Apr 13 to May 22, 2026. 2027 dates not posted (expect spring 2027)
programs.matching: Applicant contributes cash or in-kind equal to at least 25% of the grant
programs.how_to_apply: Apply through the Small Business Centre (info@smallbusinessctr.com, 613-961-0590)
programs.notes: Local intake details: https://www.smallbusinessctr.com/services/. Ask the centre whether one owner can enter two businesses (BBG and CCCL).

programs.name: Ontario Trillium Foundation Seed Grant
programs.who_can_apply: CRA-registered charities and not-for-profit corporations without share capital, with 12+ months of incorporation, operating and financial history; for-profits ineligible
programs.what_it_funds: New programs or pilots (community discussion, feasibility, research or pilot project), e.g., under the 'Prosperous People' (economic well-being) action area
programs.amount: $5,000 to $75,000 per year, up to 12 months
programs.intake: No upcoming deadline posted; the last Seed intake has closed
programs.matching: None stated; 10% held back until final report
programs.how_to_apply: Watch OTF's grant deadlines page and apply through the OTF portal when it opens
programs.notes: Requires at least 3 active board members and Board-approved financial statements. Scored on Strategy 50%, Process 25%, People 25%. Eligibility policy: https://otf.ca/node/107. Realistically, Second Chance's first eligible OTF intake is about 12 months after incorporation.

programs.name: Ontario Trillium Foundation Grow Grant
programs.who_can_apply: Registered charities and not-for-profit corporations (12+ months history); for-profits ineligible
programs.what_it_funds: Scaling a proven program
programs.amount: $50,000 to $250,000 over up to 24 months (per Mentor Works summary of OTF terms)
programs.intake: Last Grow intake closed Nov 5, 2025; next not posted
programs.how_to_apply: Apply through the OTF portal when an intake opens
programs.notes: Only after Second Chance has a track record (e.g., after a Seed-funded pilot).

programs.name: Ontario Trillium Foundation Capital Grant
programs.who_can_apply: Registered or incorporated non-profits actively operating 12+ months, delivering programs in sports and recreation, arts and culture, environment, or human and social services; for-profits ineligible
programs.what_it_funds: Equipment (fixed and non-fixed), renovations and retrofits, outdoor space improvements
programs.amount: $10,000 to $200,000, for 6 or 12 months
programs.intake: Most recent window Feb 4 to Mar 4, 2026 (closed); watch for the next window
programs.matching: None stated; quotes required for items over $5,000
programs.how_to_apply: Apply through the OTF portal when the next window opens
programs.notes: Needs 3+ board members (50% arm's length). Fixed equipment or renovations need ownership or a lease with 5+ years remaining. If Cody ever set up a separate nonprofit youth sport club, this is the main equipment grant it could use; BBG itself cannot apply.

programs.name: OTF Youth Opportunities Fund: Youth Innovations (Test / Scale) grants
programs.who_can_apply: Grassroots groups (not registered charities and not incorporated, or small non-profits with gross revenue of $50,000 or less) with an Organizational Mentor; youth 29 and under must be more than 50% of the core group (adult-initiated youth partnerships allowed for Test grants only); for-profits and registered charities ineligible
programs.what_it_funds: Projects benefiting young people aged 12-25 (12-29 for youth with disabilities, mental health or addiction needs), including justice/care well-being outcomes
programs.amount: Up to $100,000 per year for 1 to 3 years (15% of budget goes to the Organizational Mentor)
programs.intake: 2026 cycle closed (EOI Apr 15, 2026; application Jul 8, 2026). 2027 cycle not posted
programs.how_to_apply: Submit an Expression of Interest when OTF opens the next YOF cycle, with an Organizational Mentor lined up
programs.notes: Doesn't fit: Second Chance serves adults leaving the justice system (Cody, Oct 20, 2026), not a youth-led group. This is the one sizeable grant that does not require Second Chance to incorporate first, but it only fits if Second Chance focuses on youth and has youth in its core group. Must be independent of larger bodies.

programs.name: KidSport Ontario: Provincial Fund (individual child grants)
programs.who_can_apply: Families (individual children) whose income is within federal low-income guidelines plus about 30%; communities without a local chapter apply to the Provincial Fund
programs.what_it_funds: Sport registration fees (not travel or competitions)
programs.amount: Up to $250 per eligible child per calendar year
programs.intake: Rolling by program season; apply by Friday, December 4, 2026 for eligible programs running January-February 2027; processed within 30 days
programs.how_to_apply: Parent registers the child, tells the club they will apply, then applies online, by paper, mail or email with proof of income (Canada Child Benefit notice preferred)
programs.notes: BBG isn't registered with Boxing Ontario or any provincial sport body (Cody, Oct 20, 2026), so KidSport can't cover BBG classes. It would if BBG registered. Key condition: 'Sport clubs must be members of their respective Provincial Sport Organization', so BBG must be a registered club with Boxing Ontario (and/or the wrestling or judo/jiu-jitsu PSO) for its programs to qualify. KidSport's 2023 chapter list had no Hastings chapter (nearest: Kingston, Northumberland).

programs.name: Canadian Tire Jumpstart Individual Child Grants
programs.who_can_apply: Parents or guardians of children aged 4 to 18 meeting Low-Income Cut-Off (LICO) criteria; funds go to the program provider, which must be a registered business, non-profit or charity approved as a Jumpstart payee
programs.what_it_funds: Registration (and equipment) costs for sustained sport or physical activity programs: at least 5 weeks with one session per week, or camps of 5+ consecutive days
programs.amount: Up to $300 per child per year (2026), subject to chapter discretion and local demand
programs.intake: 2026 program is open; apply before the program starts; payment takes 6-8 weeks
programs.how_to_apply: Parent creates an account on the Jumpstart Individual Child Grant page and applies with a Canada Child Benefit statement and program details
programs.notes: BBG is already signed up to take Jumpstart grants (Cody, Oct 20, 2026). FAQ (https://jumpstart.canadiantire.ca/pages/faq) confirms the payee can be a 'registered business', so a for-profit gym like BBG can receive these payments once registered and verified as a payee (new payees add processing time). Some chapters have stopped accepting applications, so families should check their account.

programs.name: Jumpstart Community Development Grants (Access and Youth Development streams)
programs.who_can_apply: Registered charities, registered nonprofits or societies, registered Canadian amateur athletic associations (RCAAAs), municipalities and other qualified donees; for-profit businesses not listed
programs.what_it_funds: Access: programs that remove barriers to sport for kids and youth. Youth Development: programs using sport to build life, leadership and employment-related skills where mentorship, coaching or employment is core (ages up to 29)
programs.amount: Access up to $25,000; Youth Development up to $75,000
programs.intake: Intake 1 (programs starting in 2027) closes October 20, 2026, 11:59 pm ET. Intake 2 (programs starting Sep 1 to Dec 31, 2027) opens Mar 10, 2027 and closes Apr 7, 2027
programs.status: open (closes Oct 20, 2026); next intake Mar 10 to Apr 7, 2027
programs.matching: None stated; paid 70% on acceptance, 30% after impact report
programs.how_to_apply: Book a call with the regional Relationship Manager, then apply on the jumpstartgrants.smartsimple.ca portal
programs.notes: Weak fit: Second Chance serves adults, and Jumpstart funds kids' and youth sport. Strong fit for a combined idea: a nonprofit Second Chance running a sport-based youth employment/mentorship program with BBG coaches delivering the sport part. BBG itself cannot be the applicant. Target the March-April 2027 intake once Second Chance is incorporated.

programs.name: Community Futures (CFDC of North & Central Hastings and South Algonquin) Business Loans
programs.funder: CFDC North & Central Hastings and South Algonquin (Bancroft; FedDev-supported Community Futures)
programs.who_can_apply: Businesses and social enterprises in its service area (Town of Bancroft, Hastings Highlands, Centre Hastings, Tweed, Marmora and Lake, Madoc, Faraday, Limerick, Tudor and Cashel, Wollaston, Carlow/Mayo, South Algonquin)
programs.what_it_funds: Operating costs, equipment, inventory, leasehold improvements, commercial real estate
programs.amount: Up to $300,000 (Ready Money microloans up to $10,000); CANtrade Opportunity Fund up to $150,000 for tariff-affected businesses
programs.intake: Continuous
programs.matching: Loan; rates, terms and security set by risk; no prepayment penalties
programs.how_to_apply: Call 613-332-5564, meet a loan officer, then submit the Loan Application (or Ready Money form) with a cash flow projection
programs.notes: BBG is in the CFDC area (Bancroft). Free business advice is a good first stop for the bigger-space plans (Cody, Oct 20, 2026). Office at 26 Chemaushgon Rd, Bancroft. Second Chance fits only if it runs a social enterprise that can repay a loan. CFDC also offers free business advice.

programs.name: CFDC Young Entrepreneur Loan Fund
programs.funder: CFDC North & Central Hastings and South Algonquin
programs.who_can_apply: Business owners aged 18 to 39 in North & Central Hastings and South Algonquin
programs.what_it_funds: Business start-up or growth
programs.amount: Up to $30,000; no fees, no payments for the first year, prime + 2.5%, term up to 5 years
programs.intake: Continuous
programs.how_to_apply: Contact Carolyn Barker Brown at 613-332-5564 ext. 203
programs.notes: Cody is 18-39 (Cody, Oct 20, 2026), so he qualifies on age. Only if Cody (or a co-owner) is 39 or younger.

programs.name: CFDC Youth Business Marketing Grant
programs.funder: CFDC North & Central Hastings and South Algonquin
programs.who_can_apply: Business owners aged 18 to 39 in the CFDC area
programs.what_it_funds: One-on-one digital marketing consultation
programs.amount: Approx. $500
programs.intake: Not stated (contact office)
programs.how_to_apply: Contact Melanie Wright at 613-332-5564 ext. 210
programs.notes: Cody is 18-39 (Cody, Oct 20, 2026), so he qualifies on age. A quick win for CCCL or BBG marketing. Small, but quick to get; age 18-39 only.

programs.name: CFDC Local Initiatives Program
programs.funder: CFDC North & Central Hastings and South Algonquin
programs.who_can_apply: Incorporated not-for-profit organizations, municipalities and other incorporated community organizations in the catchment; unincorporated groups only if an incorporated partner leads
programs.what_it_funds: Incremental community economic development projects (capital or non-capital); not core operations, staff wages, basic websites, yearly festivals or construction
programs.amount: Non-repayable, normally up to $3,000
programs.intake: One project per organization per fiscal year (Apr 1 to Mar 31); projects cannot run past March 31
programs.how_to_apply: Contact the CFDC office before applying
programs.notes: Good small first grant for Second Chance (e.g., an employer-partnership launch or resume workshop series). Hastings County's resource page lists this at up to $3,500; CFDC's own page says normally up to $3,000.

programs.name: CFDC Façade Improvement Grant Program
programs.funder: CFDC North & Central Hastings and South Algonquin
programs.who_can_apply: Legally registered small or medium-sized businesses in the CFDC service area, on commercially zoned property
programs.what_it_funds: Façade improvements under a Green (environmental) or Accessibility component
programs.amount: Up to $3,000 non-repayable
programs.intake: Page still shows costs must be incurred before March 31, 2025; current round unconfirmed
programs.how_to_apply: Contact CFDC to confirm whether a current round is open
programs.notes: BBG leases its building (Cody, Oct 20, 2026): ask CFDC whether a tenant can apply (usually with the landlord's written OK). Only if BBG's building needs accessible entrances or green upgrades. Costs before approval are ineligible.

programs.name: Town of Bancroft Community Improvement Plan (incl. Tax Increment Equivalent Grant)
programs.who_can_apply: Property owners and businesses within the CIP area (details in the CIP document)
programs.what_it_funds: Revitalization and redevelopment incentives for commercial properties; Tax Increment Equivalent Grant for improvements that raise assessed value
programs.amount: Not stated on web pages; see CIP document
programs.intake: Not stated
programs.how_to_apply: Download the CIP and application form from the Town's CIP page or contact Bancroft Economic Development
programs.notes: BBG is inside Bancroft's CIP area and leases its building (Cody, Oct 20, 2026). Worth asking the Town what a tenant can apply for, especially if BBG renovates or moves to a bigger space. CIP document: https://bancroft.civicweb.net/filepro/documents/59817 ; TIEG document: https://bancroft.civicweb.net/filepro/documents/60016 (could not be read automatically). Relevant only if BBG owns or is renovating a commercial building in the CIP area.

programs.name: Town of Bancroft council grants and in-kind event support
programs.who_can_apply: Community organizations and events that request support from council (no formal published program found)
programs.what_it_funds: Cash grants and in-kind municipal services for community events
programs.amount: Historic example (2016): Rally of the Tall Pines got $5,000 cash plus $7,500 in services; Wheels/Water/Wings got $3,000 plus $10,500 in services
programs.intake: Requests reviewed in the annual budget process (2016 review was late March)
programs.how_to_apply: Send a written request to council or Economic Development ahead of budget deliberations
programs.notes: Source is a 2016 news article, not a current policy. For-profit status of CCCL may limit cash support; in-kind support (venue, arena, promotion) is the more realistic ask. Ask the Town if a current grants policy exists.

programs.name: Ontario's Highlands Tourism Organization (RTO 11) membership and Come Wander marketing partnerships
programs.who_can_apply: Businesses, organizations or individuals that operate in Ontario's Highlands and/or deliver services to visitors (membership is free for tourism participants)
programs.what_it_funds: Free marketing exposure: Come Wander content features, social posts, website features, newsletters, influencer and photo-shoot partnerships; early notice of grants; free member training
programs.amount: No cash funding currently ('None at this time' for funding opportunities)
programs.intake: Membership year-round
programs.how_to_apply: Register through the OHTO member portal (ohto.ca/become-a-member) and contact the marketing department or book a Discovery Call
programs.notes: Joining lets OHTO flag funding to CCCL when it appears (members were previously eligible for a 'TRIP' skills development funding program). Marketing programs: https://ohto.ca/programs-resources/marketing-programs

programs.name: RTO8 (Kawarthas Northumberland) Partnership Funding Program
programs.who_can_apply: Established for-profit tourism businesses (incorporated or with an active CRA business number, selling directly to consumers) in Kawartha Lakes, Northumberland, and the City and County of Peterborough; DMOs, chambers/BIAs and municipalities
programs.what_it_funds: Matched digital marketing campaigns for bookable experiences with an overnight stay (visitors travelling 40+ km), signage, studies, visual assets
programs.amount: Partner contributions of $1,500 to $14,000, matched by RTO8 (not a grant)
programs.intake: 2026-27 single intake closed Apr 6, 2026; 2027-28 not posted
programs.how_to_apply: Download and submit the Partnership Funding Program application PDF during the intake
programs.notes: CCCL is based in RTO 11 territory, so it likely only qualifies if it runs a recurring show in Peterborough or Lindsay with a local partner (e.g., a venue or DMO applicant). Pair the show with hotel packages to fit the overnight-stay focus.

programs.name: Tourism Kingston sport event funding
programs.who_can_apply: Organizers bringing sport events to Kingston; eligibility depends on event type, expected impact, length of stay and time of year
programs.what_it_funds: Offsetting event hosting costs, including accommodation support
programs.amount: Not stated
programs.intake: Not stated
programs.how_to_apply: Use the 'apply now' form on Tourism Kingston's tournament and event hosting page
programs.notes: The page does not say whether for-profit promoters qualify; ask before planning a Kingston-area show. Room nights booked by fighters, teams and fans are the likely selling point.

programs.name: United Way Hastings & Prince Edward Community Impact Fund
programs.who_can_apply: CRA qualified donees (not-for-profit charitable organizations) with a volunteer board and audited or reviewed financial statements, serving Hastings and/or Prince Edward County; for-profits excluded
programs.what_it_funds: One-year program funding under three pillars: kids be all they can be; moving people from poverty to possibility; strong and healthy communities
programs.amount: Minimum request $5,000; no maximum stated
programs.intake: Opens October 23, 2026, 8 am; training Nov 2, 2026; due December 11, 2026, 4 pm; decisions end of February 2027
programs.how_to_apply: Apply through the e-CIMPACT system after reviewing the Investment Guidelines; contact klalonde@unitedwayhpe.ca
programs.notes: Second Chance cannot meet this in the 2026-27 round; target a later round after charitable registration. Ask United Way about its Innovation Fund small grants (currently closed).

programs.name: 100 Women Who Care - Bancroft Region
programs.funder: 100 Women Who Care Bancroft Region (giving circle)
programs.who_can_apply: Registered charities serving the Bancroft region that can issue tax receipts (nominated or self-submitted, drawn from a hat)
programs.what_it_funds: Unrestricted donation pooled from members at each gathering
programs.amount: $100 per member or team per gathering; 3 gatherings a year (spring, fall, winter)
programs.intake: Three pitch rounds a year; winners wait a year before re-entering
programs.how_to_apply: Submit the charity's name to be entered in the draw
programs.notes: Source is a January 2023 local news article; confirm current details on the group's Facebook page (listed on Hastings County's business resources page).

programs.name: MLSE Foundation Community Action Grant
programs.who_can_apply: CRA qualified donees performing services in Ontario (registered charities, registered Ontario amateur athletic associations, municipalities, First Nations, etc.); organizations without that status can apply with a qualified-donee trustee
programs.what_it_funds: Youth sport and recreation programs for equity-deserving youth; primary focus Black youth, First Nations/Inuit/Métis youth, and women and girl-identified youth (gender-specific programming); emerging focus newcomer, 2SLGBTQ+ and low-income youth
programs.intake: EOI opens Nov 3, 2026 (webinar Nov 17, 2026), EOI closes Dec 15, 2026; full applications Feb 2 to Mar 2, 2027; outcomes Apr 1, 2027
programs.how_to_apply: Submit an Expression of Interest through the MLSE Foundation portal
programs.notes: BBG cannot apply as a for-profit, but a girls' or women's boxing program could be funded if a local qualified donee (e.g., a youth-serving charity) applies as lead or trustee and BBG delivers the coaching. Confirm the trustee route works for a project delivered by a for-profit.

programs.name: Community Coaching Grant (Coaches Association of Ontario and Hydro One)
programs.funder: Coaches Association of Ontario with Hydro One
programs.who_can_apply: Individual sport coaches in Ontario at any level; organizations may apply for a group of coaches if the coaches directly benefit
programs.what_it_funds: Safety training (NCCP or other safety-focused courses), replacing outdated or unsafe equipment (mats, protective gear), other safe-sport costs
programs.amount: Up to $1,000 per recipient (at least 40 grants in 2026)
programs.intake: 2026 applications closed June 5, 2026 (opened in May); 2027 dates not posted
programs.matching: None; expenses before acceptance are ineligible
programs.how_to_apply: Online application on the CAO Safe Sport 101 grant page when it reopens
programs.notes: Because individual coaches can apply, for-profit status is not a barrier here. Scoring rewards specific items and quantities, how they improve safety or access (with data), and a detailed budget. 2026 announcement: https://hydroone.mediaroom.com/2026-05-19-Coaches-Association-of-Ontario-and-Hydro-One-invest-in-safe-and-accessible-sport-with-the-2026-Community-Coaching-Grant

programs.name: The Next Play (Canadian Women & Sport, funded by Ontario)
programs.funder: Canadian Women & Sport with the Government of Ontario
programs.who_can_apply: Ontario-based sport, physical activity and recreation organizations (for-profit eligibility not stated)
programs.what_it_funds: Training on gender-inclusive program design plus a grant to run programs that engage and retain girls and gender-diverse youth
programs.amount: Earlier rounds: $1,000 honorarium for completing training plus a $4,500 project grant (2024 details); 65 organizations funded in 2025
programs.intake: Annual spring intake (2025 opened late April); 2026 recipients already announced; 2027 not posted
programs.how_to_apply: Apply through Canadian Women & Sport when the next round opens
programs.notes: Ask info@womenandsport.ca whether for-profit gyms qualify before investing time. Fits BBG's women's boxing and girls' programs.

programs.name: Canadian Women & Sport Spotlight Grant
programs.who_can_apply: Community sport and physical activity organizations (for-profit eligibility not stated)
programs.what_it_funds: Projects removing barriers for girls from priority communities (2SLGBTQIA+, Black, Indigenous, racialized, low-income, disability, newcomer)
programs.intake: Not stated
programs.how_to_apply: Check the program page or email spotlight@womenandsport.ca
programs.notes: Low-income girls in North Hastings could be the priority group; confirm eligibility of for-profit clubs.

programs.name: TELUS Friendly Future Foundation Community Boards (Ottawa and Eastern Ontario)
programs.who_can_apply: Canadian registered charities and qualified donees
programs.what_it_funds: Programs supporting youth up to age 29 facing obstacles, with health and education focus
programs.amount: Up to $20,000, single year
programs.intake: No Canadian community board deadlines listed
programs.how_to_apply: Apply through the TELUS community grants portal when the board's intake opens
programs.notes: Weak fit unless Second Chance adds a youth program: it serves adults leaving the justice system. Fits if Second Chance serves youth (e.g., youth job readiness).

programs.name: RBC Foundation community investments
programs.who_can_apply: Registered charities or other qualified donees in Canada; individuals, political groups and sports teams (unless qualified donees) ineligible
programs.what_it_funds: Initiatives that build skills for the future of work and expand inclusive opportunity
programs.amount: Requests generally up to C$500,000/year; typically no more than 20% of an organization's operating budget
programs.intake: No deadlines listed
programs.matching: RBC funds at most ~20% of operating budget
programs.how_to_apply: Apply through RBC's Community Investments page for Canada
programs.notes: Seed funding requests from organizations under 5 years old may use unaudited statements. Long shot for a new charity; better after a year of results.

not_eligible.name: Experience Ontario 2026/2027 (Established Events and Capacity Building streams)
not_eligible.why: CCCL shows don't qualify: events must run at least two consecutive days with 5+ hours of programming each day. The program also excludes sporting competitions not marketed to tourists, events of a primarily commercial nature, and sole proprietorships and partnerships as applicants. The 2026 intake closed Dec 16, 2025. Note: Experience Ontario is the province's current festival/event program.

not_eligible.name: Reconnect Festival and Event Program (Ontario)
not_eligible.why: No current Reconnect intake found. It was a pandemic-recovery program, and Ontario's current festival/event funding is Experience Ontario (see above). Not available to CCCL.

not_eligible.name: Ontario Sport Hosting Program 2026-27
not_eligible.why: For-profit applicants are ineligible, and events must be national or international, sanctioned by listed national sport organizations or international federations (no MMA body is listed). CCCL can't apply.

not_eligible.name: Eastern Ontario Development Fund (EODF)
not_eligible.why: Business projects need 3+ years of operation, at least 5 employees in rural areas, $200,000+ investment and 5 new jobs (or a 30% increase). Personal services are excluded. Community projects must be led by municipalities, economic development or sector organizations. Not realistic for BBG or CCCL. (Hastings is in the program area; next deadline Jan 21, 2027.)

not_eligible.name: FedDev Ontario Tourism Growth Program (southern Ontario)
not_eligible.why: Closed and no longer accepting applications. It covered 2023-24 to 2025-26. Watch for a successor program; incorporated tourism SMEs were eligible (repayable contributions).

not_eligible.name: FedDev Ontario funding for businesses (e.g., Business Scale-up and Productivity)
not_eligible.why: Businesses must be for-profit, incorporated for at least 3 years, and have at least 5 full-time employees. BBG and CCCL likely fall short.

not_eligible.name: FedDev Build Communities Strong Fund - Local Impact Stream
not_eligible.why: Intake is paused. It is for community infrastructure projects, not small businesses.

not_eligible.name: Sport Canada Community Sport for All Initiative
not_eligible.why: Closed. Only national-level incorporated not-for-profits could apply. Community groups get this money indirectly through funded national organizations such as Jumpstart.

not_eligible.name: ESDC Youth Employment and Skills Strategy - Strategic Collaboration
ESDC Team Canada Strong Youth Placements
not_eligible.why: The expression of interest closes Oct 23, 2026. It funds large trades and construction placement projects (up to $15M/year), and for-profits are allowed only for non-commercial activity. Second Chance is not yet incorporated and the project scale doesn't fit.

not_eligible.name: Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund - Stream 1 (Repair and Rehabilitation)
not_eligible.why: For-profit organizations are not listed as eligible (only municipalities, Indigenous organizations, local services boards and not-for-profits). BBG can only use Stream 2 (new builds).

not_eligible.name: Ontario Trillium Foundation (all Community Investments streams) for BBG or CCCL
not_eligible.why: OTF's eligibility policy lists for-profit organizations, individuals, and organizations with less than 12 months of incorporation, operating and financial history as ineligible. Only a nonprofit (e.g., Second Chance after incorporation) can apply.

not_eligible.name: ParticipACTION Community Challenge grants
not_eligible.why: For-profit organizations are ineligible, so BBG can't apply. The 2026 intake closed Feb 10, 2026. A nonprofit partner could apply for up to $1,000 for June physical-activity programming.

not_eligible.name: Summer Company (Ontario)
not_eligible.why: Only for students aged 15-29 starting their own summer business (up to $3,000), so it doesn't fund BBG or CCCL. A BBG teen could use it to start their own business, but the gym can't apply.

not_eligible.name: City of Peterborough Community Grants
not_eligible.why: For-profit businesses are ineligible, and applicants must be nonprofits or neighbourhood groups operating mainly within Peterborough city limits.

not_eligible.name: City of Kawartha Lakes Local Economic Development Support Grant
not_eligible.why: Only for non-profit organizations within the City of Kawartha Lakes. The 2026 intake closed Jan 15, 2026.

not_eligible.name: Haliburton County Development Corporation (HCDC) loans
not_eligible.why: HCDC only serves businesses and not-for-profits in Haliburton County. CCCL qualifies only if it is based there; Bancroft-based businesses use the Bancroft CFDC instead.

not_eligible.name: TIAO Tourism Workforce Sustainability Program
not_eligible.why: The program has officially wrapped up. It was one-year SDF funding.

not_eligible.name: Public Safety Canada Grants and Contributions Program to Voluntary Organizations (community reintegration)
not_eligible.why: Only for incorporated not-for-profits offering corrections, conditional release or reintegration programming. The 2025-26 call closed Jan 23, 2026. Second Chance can consider a future call only once incorporated and if it serves justice-involved people.

tips: Canada Summer Jobs 2027 opens Oct 27, 2026 at 9:00 am ET. Have the CRA business number and payroll deductions account ready. Jobs must be 30-40 hours/week for 6-16 consecutive weeks. Private employers get up to 50% of minimum wage with no MERCs; not-for-profits get up to 100% plus MERCs. Write the application to the riding's local priorities (2026 priorities for Hastings-Lennox and Addington-Tyendinaga included community events and local/regional tourism development). (canada.ca CSJ applicant guide; CFIB CSJ page; CSJ local priorities page)

KidSport only pays for clubs that are members of their Provincial Sport Organization. Boxing Ontario club registration needs at least one NCCP Level 1 Instruction Beginner coach, a safety inspection, and staff registered with Boxing Ontario; registration runs to Dec 31 each year. BBG isn't registered (Cody, Oct 20, 2026). Decide whether to register: it's the only way families could use KidSport at BBG (Dec 4, 2026 deadline for Jan-Feb 2027 programs). (kidsportcanada.ca/ontario/provincial-fund; boxingontario.com becoming a registered club)

Structure kids' programs as sessions of at least 5 weeks (one or more classes per week) or camps of at least 5 consecutive days so they qualify for Jumpstart individual grants. BBG is already a Jumpstart payee (Cody, Oct 2026); cheques go to the provider, not the family. Families should apply before the program starts. (jumpstart.canadiantire.ca individual-child-grants and FAQ)

OTF requires nonprofits to have 12 months of incorporation, operating and financial history, at least 3 board members, and Board-approved financial statements. Incorporate Second Chance as early as possible so the 12-month clock starts. Seed applications are scored Strategy 50%, Process 25%, People 25%. (otf.ca eligibility policy and Seed grant page)

Several funders (MLSE Foundation, RBC, TELUS, United Way, 100 Women Who Care) require qualified-donee status: a registered charity, or a registered Canadian amateur athletic association for sport. MLSE lets non-qualified groups apply through a qualified-donee trustee. Partnering with an existing local charity as lead or trustee is the fastest route for youth or employment projects. (mlsefoundation.org community grants; rbc.com apply for funding; telus.com community grants; unitedwayhpe.ca/funding)

Jumpstart Community Development Grants recommend booking a call with your regional Relationship Manager before applying. Its Youth Development stream (up to $75,000) funds sport programs where coaching, mentorship or employment is core, which matches a Second Chance + BBG youth employment program. Next intake opens Mar 10, 2027. (jumpstart.canadiantire.ca/pages/community-development-grants)

Rural Ontario Development business funding is first-come, first-served, and each business gets only one successful application. Costs incurred before the project's effective date are ineligible. Fill the form in Adobe Acrobat (not a browser), email it to RODProgram@ontario.ca, and register on Transfer Payment Ontario first. The next window is Jan 18 to Feb 25, 2027. (ontario.ca ROD page and business development application form)

Starter Company Plus requires a cash or in-kind contribution of at least 25% of the grant. Hastings County businesses apply through the Small Business Centre in Belleville (2026 intake was Apr 13 to May 22), so plan a business plan and cash flow for a spring 2027 intake. (ontario.ca/page/starter-company-plus; smallbusinessctr.com/services)

CFDC loan applications need the amount, its purpose and how it helps the business, a meeting with staff, the Loan Application (or Ready Money form under $10,000), and a cash flow projection. Owners aged 18-39 can get the Young Entrepreneur Loan with no payments in year one. (community-futures.ca business loans)

Ontario Job Grant: employers with under 100 employees pay at least one-sixth of training costs. Training must be from an eligible third-party provider with 2+ years of experience delivering it, and the employer must have operated in Ontario for at least a year. Up to $15,000 with no employer share is possible when training an unemployed new hire, which could pair well with Second Chance clients hired by partner employers. (ontario.ca/page/ontario-job-grant)

The Coaches Association of Ontario Community Coaching Grant lets individual coaches apply (up to $1,000 for mats, protective gear or safety training). Each BBG coach could apply separately when it reopens (2026 window closed June 5). Purchases made before acceptance are not reimbursed. (safesport101.coachesontario.ca/grant)

The Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund caps for-profit applicants at 25% provincial cost share, requires audited financial statements and a corporate structure document, and closes Dec 22, 2026. Only pursue it if a new or expanded BBG facility is planned. (ontario.ca CSRIF Stream 2)

The County of Haliburton is hosting a Funders Forum on November 5, 2026 for local businesses, nonprofits and community groups, a chance to meet funders relevant to CCCL's Haliburton shows. (haliburtoncounty.ca home page)

United Way Hastings & Prince Edward: applications open Oct 23, 2026, training session Nov 2, due Dec 11, 2026 through e-CIMPACT. Minimum request is $5,000, and audited or reviewed statements plus a volunteer board are required, so this is a goal for Second Chance after it becomes a charity. (unitedwayhpe.ca/funding)

Track where CCCL ticket buyers come from (postal codes). Tourism funders define a visitor or tourist as someone travelling 40+ km (Experience Ontario, RTO8), and this data is what tourism partners and municipalities will ask for. (EO26 guidelines; rto8.com partnership program)

MLSE Foundation Community Action Grant: expression of interest opens Nov 3, 2026, info webinar Nov 17, closes Dec 15, 2026. Women- and girl-identified youth programming is a primary focus, which suits BBG's women's boxing if delivered with a qualified-donee lead. (mlsefoundation.org)
